summary: PDF dashboard export removes tracing hooks and truncates trace IDs for multi-page exports
description: Issue summary: Customer reported that when they export a large dashboard (5+ panels, multiple pages) to PDF via the Console 'Export' action, the generated PDF strips the tracing hook anchor tags and truncates trace IDs in panels and alert notification samples. Impact: - Customers cannot click through from PDF snapshots or attached alerts to the live trace in Console. - For enterprise customers using PDFs for runbooks/postmortems this breaks traceability and increases incident mean time to resolution. - Affects scheduled snapshot exports and manual on-demand exports when result spans multiple PDF pages. Environment: - Prod (us-east). Enterprise org: BrightCart Inc. Multiple dashboards with long query templates and tracehook params. Steps to reproduce: 1) Go to Console -> Dashboards -> Select a dashboard with 6+ panels and a tracehook integration (panels that render 'View trace' links). 2) Click 'Export' -> select 'PDF' -> select 'Include annotations and links' -> Export. 3) Open the resulting PDF and inspect the panels spread across pages 2-4. 4) Try to click any trace link or copy the trace ID from the PDF. Observed behavior: - Anchor tags for tracehook links are removed on page boundary regions (links appear as plain text). - Trace IDs are truncated mid-string (e.g., "abc123...ef") or appended with ellipses when crossing a page break. - Scheduled snapshots (nightly) also produce PDFs with the same issue. Expected behavior: - PDF export should preserve tracehook anchor hrefs and full trace IDs so links are actionable or copyable. Attachments: - Dashboard URL: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/brightcart/dashboards/ops-runbook - Sample exported PDF uploaded by customer (attached to ticket). Logs / snippets: - Export service job log (excerpt): job_id=exp-20260305-79a2 status=completed pages=6 render_engine=chromium-v1 warn: page-break-heuristic triggered for panel_id=panel-17 info: svg-to-png fallback for panel-17 due to font-metrics - Console tracehook audit: tracehook_id=th-004 linked_id=trace:abc123def456ghi789 ttl=7d - Rendered HTML snippet before export (customer-provided): View trace - Rendered PDF text shows: "View trace" (no link) and "abc123def4..."
investigation:
Initial triage by Support: 2026-03-05
- Reproduced internally using BrightCart dashboard with synthetic tracehook links.
- Problem localized to the PDF rendering pipeline when panel content spans a page break.

Eng investigation (Rendering team): 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-08
Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: Page-break CSS in export template strips anchor tags during HTML->PDF conversion. Reproduced when forced page breaks applied; anchors becoming non-clickable in chromium headless snapshot.
- Hypothesis B: Long href query strings are being rewritten by the SVG-to-image conversion stage (we convert certain panels to PNGs to improve fidelity) which strips link metadata. Confirmed: panels converted to raster images lose hyperlink metadata.
- Hypothesis C: Scheduled snapshot flow runs a different conversion path that applies text-truncation for long contiguous strings across linewraps. Reproduced in scheduled job logs (page-break-heuristic warning).

Findings:
- Primary cause: Panels that are rendered as raster images (SVG->PNG) for export lose anchor metadata. When the rendering engine chooses rasterization (fonts or complex CSS), the resulting image is embedded and any link overlay falls back to plain text.
- Secondary cause: Our PDF post-processing step attempts to create text-layer link annotations for visible trace IDs, but the algorithm splits long IDs at page boundaries and inserts ellipses when a single token crosses the page gap.
- The issue is only triggered for multi-page exports where a panel element is split by a page break or converted to raster due to font/CSS complexity.

Related code areas:
- pdf-export-service: html_renderer.py (svg_to_png), pdf_annotator.py (link_restitcher).

Repro command used by Eng:
- export-cli --dashboard ops-runbook --format pdf --force-page-breaks --headless-chrome=chromium-v1

Relevant PR discovered during search: an open PR that attempted to optimize rasterization heuristics and inadvertently removed link preservation in the png conversion path (PR referenced in related_github_prs).
comments: 2026-03-05 - BrightCart (Customer): We've attached a PDF we generated last night; links are all dead and trace IDs get cut. This is blocking our SRE rotation documentation.
2026-03-05 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Reproducing steps requested and escalated to Rendering team. SLA P1 acknowledged; aiming for first ENG response within 24h.

2026-03-06 - Diego Alvarez (Rendering): Confirmed reproduction. Working on a fix to preserve link metadata for panels that go through svg_to_png. Temporary workaround: disable 'High fidelity rasterization' in export settings for now.

2026-03-07 - Diego Alvarez (Rendering): Implemented patch to carry anchor metadata into the image->pdf pipeline by exporting a sidecar JSON of link boxes and restoring them during annotation. Running CI and staging validation.
2026-03-09 - QA (Verena Kline): Regression tests added for multi-page exports with tracehooks. Verified with BrightCart sample dashboard. Links preserved in exported PDF for all tested cases.

2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Deploy to prod verified with customer. BrightCart confirmed nightly scheduled PDF now includes working trace links. Customer has accepted resolution and will follow up if anything else appears.
resolution:
Root cause: Export pipeline rasterized some dashboard panels to PNG which removed anchor/link metadata; post-processing algorithm then attempted to reconstruct links but truncated IDs at page boundaries.

Fix applied:
- Patch applied to pdf-export-service (PR #482): when svg->png conversion is used, the renderer now emits a link-map sidecar (coordinates + href) which pdf_annotator now consumes to restore clickable link annotations.
- Improved link-restitcher to handle tokens crossing page boundaries by reconstructing full trace IDs from adjacent text nodes instead of inserting ellipses.

Rollout and verification notes:
- Staging rollout 2026-03-08; smoke tests passed.
- Prod rollout 2026-03-09 (canary -> full).
- BrightCart confirmed fix in nightly snapshot 2026-03-10.

Workarounds provided to customer before fix:
- Export as PNG per-panel or disable 'High fidelity rasterization' in Export options to keep HTML link overlays.
- Use 'Share snapshot' link from Console (preserves live links) instead of PDF.

Follow-ups:
- Add unit tests covering link preservation for multi-page exports and scheduled snapshots.
- Monitor pdf-export-service error rates and scheduled snapshot failures for 2 weeks.
- Postmortem doc created and linked in Confluence.
